title: The Champion Change Check
subtitle: Recheck one commitment before keeping the old plan
intro_text: Use in the existing account record with the relevant customer people. Keep private details out of public copies.

sections.title: Name the commitment
sections.instruction: What is the customer trying to do next? Record the agreed goal, next task and date. Confirm whether that priority still stands.

sections.title: Find the missing contribution
sections.instruction: What did the departing person enable? Separate knowledge of the work, willingness to help and authority over time or funding. Mark unconfirmed roles as unknown.

sections.title: Choose what happens next
sections.instruction: Continue if the required people agree. Change the step if the goal survives but the route changed. Hold only the affected request if its decision owner is missing; name the next action and date.

example.heading: Example: a second-department rollout
example.label: Fictional example, not a customer result.
rows: Run a workflow trial with the next team
example.interpretation: A new contact can help arrange the conversation. The next team's manager still needs to agree test time before the trial date is confirmed.

prompt:
Next customer commitment / date: [ ]
What the departing person enabled: [ ]
Knowledge / willingness / authority now: [confirmed / unknown]
Missing decision and person who can make it: [ ]
Continue / change / hold which request: [ ]
Next action, owner and customer update date: [ ]
next_action: Run on one commitment. Update the existing plan with what current customer people actually confirm. Do not infer a renewal probability from the departure.
methodology: Original editorial decision aid, informed by public GitLab and Microsoft role guidance. Not a measured retention intervention.
